newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - APRIL 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - APRIL 29.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:
--Thirty-four people died in a total of 267 accidents on Greece's roads during the Easter break, with a further 358 injured.
--Representing Greece, Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos yesterday baptised the daughter of Tassos Isaak, clubbed to death during last summer's violence on the green line in Cyprus.

--The General Confederation of Workers of Greece has responded with seven "ayes" and seven "nays" to the government's proposals on changes to the job market. The dissent in the union movement on the positions, however, is best evidenced by the fact that Labour Day on May 1 will be celebrated by two different rallies.
--Defence Minister Akis Tsohatzopoulos met with the Albanian leadership during his trip to the neighbouring country to visit Greek troops for Easter.
--A new study by the European Union shows that Greece is the EU's poorest country and the the poorest region is Epirus.
--A new study shows that 98.5 percent of Greece's 1,258 beaches are clean and appropriate for bathing.

--Changes to recipients of pensions from pension funds are in the offing as of 1998, in line with laws passed during the New Democracy administration in 1992. The changes include increased retirement age and ceilings on lump sump payments.
--The announcement of the appointment of 7,000 civil servants is only a matter of days, according to reports.

--Waged labour will be a thing of the past as Prime Minister Costas Simitis visions of a new job market based on "work contracts" comes to pass. The premier, reports say, plans to introduce direct contracts between employee and employer that will do away with the basic wage.
--Hundreds of farmers will face court over the disruption caused to national transport links during the 25-day blockade late last year.
--Traffic police are on the lookout for the individual throwing rocks on the Athens-Corinth national road who has so far caused damage to 50 vehicles. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
